qualitative.gate_2_reason: Discretionary upscale and luxury lodging deferrable during economic downturns; highly cyclical travel demand.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 2 (Discretionary & Deferrable Cyclical, REJECT). Upper-upscale and luxury hotel REIT portfolio (Ritz-Carlton, Westin, Marriott, Hyatt) exposed to volatile business convention and leisure transient travel cycles, which are easily postponed or cancelled during recessions. Does not meet the essential Western need or entrenched daily habit standard.
qualitative.evidence: Host Hotels & Resorts is the largest US lodging REIT, owning ~74-76 luxury and upper-upscale properties (~42,000 rooms) managed by third parties (Marriott, Hyatt, Hilton). While FY2024-FY2025 revenue reached $5.68B-$6.11B with net income of $707M-$776M and carrying debt of ~$5.08B, hotel real estate economics are characterized by low multi-cycle returns on invested capital (10-year median ROIC ~5.5%), ongoing renovation capital requirements, and extreme demand sensitivity during recessions and travel freezes. Luxury lodging is non-essential and easily deferred, disqualifying it at Gate 2.
